functional.title: Verify API documentation page is accessible and loads correctly
preconditions: User is logged into the application with a valid account
API documentation has been published and deployed to the documentation portal
User has at least 'Viewer' or 'Developer' role permissions
Browser is a supported version (Chrome 90+, Firefox 88+, Edge 90+, Safari 14+)

steps.action: Navigate to the main application dashboard and locate the 'Documentation' or 'API Docs' link in the top navigation bar or sidebar menu
steps.expectedResult: A 'Documentation' or 'API Docs' navigation link is visible and clickable

steps.action: Click on the 'API Documentation' link
steps.expectedResult: The API documentation page loads within 3 seconds, displaying the documentation landing page with a table of contents, API overview section, and version information

steps.action: Verify the page structure includes sections for: Introduction, Authentication, Endpoints, Request/Response formats, Error codes, and Rate limiting
steps.expectedResult: All major sections are present in the table of contents and are navigable via anchor links on the left sidebar or top navigation

steps.action: Scroll through the entire API documentation page from top to bottom
steps.expectedResult: All content renders correctly without broken layouts, missing images, or placeholder text. Code examples are syntax-highlighted and properly formatted

steps.action: Verify the API version number is displayed prominently on the documentation page header
steps.expectedResult: The current API version (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.0') is clearly displayed in the page header or breadcrumb area

postconditions: API documentation page remains loaded and fully accessible
User session remains active and authenticated
No console errors or 404 resource loading failures in browser developer tools

functional.title: Verify User Guide page is accessible and loads all sections correctly
preconditions: User is logged into the application with a valid account
User guide content has been published and is available on the documentation portal
User has at least 'Viewer' role permissions

steps.action: Navigate to the main application dashboard and locate the 'User Guide' link in the navigation menu, help menu, or footer
steps.expectedResult: A 'User Guide' link is visible and accessible from the main navigation or help section

steps.action: Click on the 'User Guide' link
steps.expectedResult: The User Guide page loads within 3 seconds, displaying a structured guide with a table of contents, getting started section, and chapter/section navigation

steps.action: Verify the User Guide includes the following sections: Getting Started, Account Setup, Core Features, Configuration, Troubleshooting, and FAQ
steps.expectedResult: All expected sections are listed in the table of contents and each section link navigates to the corresponding content

steps.action: Click on the 'Getting Started' section link in the table of contents
steps.expectedResult: The page scrolls to or navigates to the Getting Started section, which contains step-by-step instructions for new users with screenshots or diagrams

steps.action: Verify that all images, diagrams, and screenshots within the User Guide load correctly
steps.expectedResult: All visual assets render properly with appropriate alt text, no broken image icons, and images are relevant to the surrounding text content

postconditions: User Guide page is fully loaded with all sections accessible
User can navigate back to the main application without issues
Browser history correctly records the User Guide page visit for back-button navigation

functional.title: Verify API documentation lists all endpoints with correct HTTP methods, paths, and descriptions
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page
API documentation reflects the latest deployed API version
User has 'Developer' or 'Admin' role permissions
At least 5 API endpoints are documented

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Endpoints' or 'API Reference' section of the API documentation
steps.expectedResult: A comprehensive list of all API endpoints is displayed, grouped by resource or functional area (e.g., Users, Projects, Reports)

steps.action: For each endpoint listed, verify that the HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) is clearly indicated with color-coded badges or labels
steps.expectedResult: Each endpoint displays its HTTP method with visual differentiation (e.g., GET in green, POST in blue, DELETE in red) and the full URL path (e.g., '/api/v1/users/{id}')

steps.action: Click on a specific GET endpoint (e.g., 'GET /api/v1/users') to expand its details
steps.expectedResult: The endpoint detail section expands showing: description, path parameters, query parameters, request headers, example request, example response (with JSON body), and HTTP status codes

steps.action: Click on a specific POST endpoint (e.g., 'POST /api/v1/users') to expand its details
steps.expectedResult: The endpoint detail section shows: description, request body schema with field names, types, required/optional flags, example request payload in JSON format, and example success/error responses

steps.action: Verify that each endpoint includes documented response status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 500)
steps.expectedResult: Each endpoint lists applicable HTTP response status codes with descriptions of when each code is returned and example response bodies for both success and error scenarios

steps.action: Cross-reference at least 3 documented endpoints against the actual running API by making test calls (using a tool like Postman or the built-in 'Try It' feature if available)
steps.expectedResult: The actual API responses match the documented request/response formats, status codes, and field names exactly

postconditions: All endpoints are verified as accurately documented
No discrepancies found between documentation and actual API behavior
User remains on the API documentation page with all sections accessible

functional.title: Verify API documentation includes authentication and authorization details
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page
Authentication section exists in the documentation
The API uses token-based authentication (e.g., Bearer token, API key, or OAuth 2.0)

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Authentication' section of the API documentation via the table of contents or sidebar navigation
steps.expectedResult: The Authentication section loads and displays detailed information about the authentication mechanism used by the API

steps.action: Verify the documentation explains how to obtain an authentication token or API key, including the endpoint URL, required credentials, and example request
steps.expectedResult: Step-by-step instructions are provided for obtaining authentication credentials, including: the token endpoint (e.g., 'POST /api/v1/auth/token'), required fields (username, password, client_id), and a complete cURL or HTTP example

steps.action: Verify the documentation explains how to include the authentication token in subsequent API requests
steps.expectedResult: Clear instructions show the required header format (e.g., 'Authorization: Bearer <token>') with an example request demonstrating the header in use

steps.action: Verify the documentation describes token expiration, refresh mechanisms, and error responses for expired/invalid tokens
steps.expectedResult: Documentation includes: token TTL (e.g., '3600 seconds'), refresh token flow if applicable, and example 401 Unauthorized response body for expired or invalid tokens

steps.action: Verify the documentation describes role-based access control and which endpoints require which permission levels
steps.expectedResult: A permissions matrix or per-endpoint authorization notes indicate which roles (e.g., Admin, Developer, Viewer) can access which endpoints, and 403 Forbidden response examples are provided

postconditions: Authentication documentation is complete and accurate
User understands how to authenticate against the API based solely on the documentation
All authentication examples use placeholder values and do not expose real credentials

functional.title: Verify search functionality within API documentation and User Guide
preconditions: User is on the documentation portal (API docs or User Guide)
A search bar or search feature is available on the documentation page
Documentation content has been indexed for search

steps.action: Locate the search bar on the documentation page (typically in the top-right corner or sidebar)
steps.expectedResult: A search input field is visible with a placeholder text such as 'Search documentation...' or a magnifying glass icon

steps.action: Type 'authentication' into the search bar and press Enter or wait for auto-complete results
steps.expectedResult: Search results appear within 2 seconds, listing all documentation sections and pages that contain the term 'authentication', with highlighted matching text snippets

steps.action: Click on the first search result
steps.expectedResult: The user is navigated to the correct section of the documentation where the search term appears, and the matching text is highlighted or scrolled into view

steps.action: Clear the search bar and type a specific endpoint path such as '/api/v1/users' and press Enter
steps.expectedResult: Search results display the relevant endpoint documentation page(s) that reference the '/api/v1/users' path

steps.action: Clear the search bar and type a nonsensical string such as 'xyzzy12345zzz' and press Enter
steps.expectedResult: A 'No results found' message is displayed with a suggestion to refine the search query or browse the table of contents

steps.action: Test search with partial terms by typing 'auth' (partial match for 'authentication' and 'authorization')
steps.expectedResult: Search results include pages containing both 'authentication' and 'authorization' and any other terms starting with or containing 'auth'

postconditions: Search functionality returns accurate and relevant results
User can navigate back to the main documentation page after searching
Search history or recent searches are not persisted in a way that exposes sensitive information

functional.title: Verify navigation between API documentation sections using table of contents and breadcrumbs
preconditions: User is on the API documentation landing page
Documentation has at least 5 distinct sections with nested subsections
Table of contents sidebar or navigation panel is visible

steps.action: Verify the table of contents (TOC) is displayed on the left sidebar or as a collapsible navigation panel
steps.expectedResult: TOC is visible with all top-level sections listed. Sections with subsections show expand/collapse indicators (arrows or +/- icons)

steps.action: Click on a top-level section in the TOC (e.g., 'Endpoints') that has subsections
steps.expectedResult: The section expands to reveal its subsections (e.g., 'Users', 'Projects', 'Reports') and the main content area navigates to or highlights the selected section

steps.action: Click on a nested subsection (e.g., 'Users' under 'Endpoints')
steps.expectedResult: The content area scrolls to or loads the 'Users' endpoint documentation. The TOC highlights the current section and subsection to indicate the user's location

steps.action: Verify breadcrumb navigation is displayed at the top of the content area (e.g., 'Home > API Documentation > Endpoints > Users')
steps.expectedResult: Breadcrumbs are displayed showing the full navigation path. Each breadcrumb segment is a clickable link

steps.action: Click on the 'API Documentation' breadcrumb link
steps.expectedResult: The user is navigated back to the API Documentation landing page, and the TOC resets to show the top-level view

steps.action: Use the browser's back button to return to the previously viewed subsection
steps.expectedResult: The browser navigates back to the 'Users' subsection, and the TOC correctly highlights the current position

postconditions: Navigation between sections works consistently via TOC, breadcrumbs, and browser history
The current section is always clearly indicated in the TOC
URL updates to reflect the current section for bookmarking and sharing purposes

functional.title: Verify API documentation code examples can be copied to clipboard
preconditions: User is on an API endpoint detail page that contains code examples
Code examples include at least cURL, JSON request body, and JSON response body samples
Browser supports the Clipboard API

steps.action: Navigate to a specific API endpoint detail page (e.g., 'POST /api/v1/users') that contains code examples
steps.expectedResult: Code examples are displayed in formatted code blocks with syntax highlighting and a 'Copy' button or icon in the top-right corner of each code block

steps.action: Click the 'Copy' button on the cURL example code block
steps.expectedResult: A visual confirmation appears (e.g., the button text changes to 'Copied!' or a green checkmark appears) and the complete cURL command is copied to the system clipboard

steps.action: Open a text editor or terminal and paste (Ctrl+V / Cmd+V) the copied content
steps.expectedResult: The pasted content exactly matches the cURL example shown in the documentation, including all headers, URL, and request body with proper formatting

steps.action: Return to the documentation page and click the 'Copy' button on a JSON response example
steps.expectedResult: The JSON response example is copied to the clipboard with proper formatting, indentation, and all fields intact

steps.action: Verify that code examples are available in multiple languages/formats if a language selector is present (e.g., cURL, Python, JavaScript, Java)
steps.expectedResult: Clicking different language tabs updates the code example to the selected language while maintaining the same API call logic and parameters

postconditions: All code examples are copyable and paste correctly into external tools
Copied code examples are syntactically valid and can be executed with minimal modification (replacing placeholder values)
Copy button visual feedback resets after a few seconds

functional.title: Verify User Guide includes step-by-step workflows with screenshots
preconditions: User is on the User Guide page
User Guide contains at least 3 workflow tutorials (e.g., account setup, creating a project, generating a report)
Screenshots and visual aids have been uploaded and linked in the guide

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Getting Started' or first workflow section of the User Guide
steps.expectedResult: The section displays a numbered step-by-step workflow with clear headings for each step (e.g., 'Step 1: Create Your Account', 'Step 2: Configure Your Profile')

steps.action: Verify each step includes descriptive text explaining the action to take
steps.expectedResult: Each step contains 1-3 paragraphs of clear, concise instructions written in plain language, specifying exact button names, menu locations, and field labels

steps.action: Verify each step includes a relevant screenshot or diagram
steps.expectedResult: Screenshots are embedded inline with the step text, are high-resolution, clearly show the relevant UI area, and have annotations (arrows, highlights, or callout boxes) pointing to the relevant elements

steps.action: Click on a screenshot to verify if it supports zoom/enlarge functionality
steps.expectedResult: Clicking the screenshot opens a larger version in a lightbox or modal overlay, allowing the user to see fine details. A close button or clicking outside the modal dismisses it

steps.action: Follow the documented workflow steps in the actual application to verify accuracy
steps.expectedResult: The steps in the User Guide match the actual application flow exactly — button names, menu locations, field labels, and UI layout match what is described and shown in screenshots

steps.action: Navigate to a different workflow section (e.g., 'Creating a Project') and repeat verification
steps.expectedResult: The second workflow section also contains accurate step-by-step instructions with corresponding screenshots that match the current application UI

postconditions: All workflow sections contain accurate, up-to-date instructions matching the current application version
All screenshots are current and reflect the latest UI design
No placeholder text (e.g., 'TODO', 'Lorem ipsum') exists in any section

functional.title: Verify API documentation error codes section is comprehensive and accurate
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page
An 'Error Codes' or 'Error Handling' section exists in the documentation
The API returns standardized error response formats

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Error Codes' or 'Error Handling' section of the API documentation
steps.expectedResult: A dedicated section is displayed listing all possible API error codes in a structured table or list format

steps.action: Verify the error codes table includes columns for: HTTP Status Code, Error Code (application-specific), Error Message, and Description/Resolution
steps.expectedResult: The table contains at minimum the following HTTP status codes: 400 (Bad Request), 401 (Unauthorized), 403 (Forbidden), 404 (Not Found), 409 (Conflict), 422 (Unprocessable Entity), 429 (Too Many Requests), 500 (Internal Server Error)

steps.action: Verify each error code entry includes an example JSON error response body
steps.expectedResult: Each error code shows an example response like: {"error": {"code": "INVALID_PARAMETER", "message": "The 'email' field must be a valid email address", "details": [...]}}

steps.action: Verify the documentation explains the standard error response schema/structure
steps.expectedResult: A clear description of the error response format is provided, including field definitions for 'code', 'message', 'details', and any other standard fields, with data types specified

steps.action: Trigger an actual API error (e.g., send a request with missing required fields) and compare the response to the documented format
steps.expectedResult: The actual API error response matches the documented error response format exactly, including field names, structure, and the specific error code/message for the triggered error condition

postconditions: All documented error codes are accurate and match actual API behavior
Error response format documentation is consistent across all endpoint sections
Developers can use the error codes section to implement proper error handling in their client applications

functional.title: Verify API documentation includes rate limiting information
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page
The API implements rate limiting
A 'Rate Limiting' section exists in the documentation

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Rate Limiting' section of the API documentation
steps.expectedResult: The Rate Limiting section is displayed with clear information about API usage limits

steps.action: Verify the documentation specifies rate limit values (e.g., requests per minute/hour) for different tiers or roles
steps.expectedResult: Rate limits are clearly stated, e.g., '100 requests per minute for standard users, 1000 requests per minute for premium users', with limits broken down by endpoint category if applicable

steps.action: Verify the documentation explains rate limit response headers (e.g., X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset)
steps.expectedResult: A table or list describes each rate limit header, its meaning, and example values (e.g., 'X-RateLimit-Remaining: 95' means 95 requests remaining in the current window)

steps.action: Verify the documentation describes the 429 Too Many Requests response and recommended retry behavior
steps.expectedResult: Documentation explains that a 429 status code is returned when the rate limit is exceeded, includes an example response body, and recommends using the 'Retry-After' header value or exponential backoff strategy

postconditions: Rate limiting documentation is complete and actionable for API consumers
Developers understand how to monitor and handle rate limits based on the documentation
Rate limit values documented match the actual API configuration

functional.title: Verify documentation versioning and version selector functionality
preconditions: User is on the documentation portal
At least 2 versions of the API documentation exist (e.g., v1.0 and v2.0)
A version selector dropdown or toggle is available on the documentation page

steps.action: Locate the version selector on the documentation page (typically in the header or sidebar)
steps.expectedResult: A version selector dropdown is visible showing the current documentation version (e.g., 'v2.0 (latest)')

steps.action: Click on the version selector dropdown to view available versions
steps.expectedResult: A dropdown list appears showing all available documentation versions (e.g., 'v2.0 (latest)', 'v1.0') with the current version highlighted or checked

steps.action: Select an older version (e.g., 'v1.0') from the dropdown
steps.expectedResult: The documentation content updates to reflect the v1.0 API documentation. The version selector now shows 'v1.0' as the active version, and a banner or notice may appear indicating the user is viewing an older version

steps.action: Verify the older version documentation shows endpoints and features specific to that version
steps.expectedResult: The v1.0 documentation shows only endpoints and features available in v1.0, and does not include v2.0-specific additions or changes

steps.action: Switch back to the latest version using the version selector
steps.expectedResult: The documentation updates to the latest version content, the version selector shows the latest version, and any 'older version' banner is removed

postconditions: Version switching works correctly and displays version-appropriate content
URL updates to include the version identifier for bookmarking (e.g., '/docs/v1.0/endpoints')
The latest version is always the default when first accessing the documentation

functional.title: Verify User Guide FAQ section provides answers to common questions
preconditions: User is on the User Guide page
An FAQ section exists with at least 10 questions and answers
FAQ items use an accordion or expandable format

steps.action: Navigate to the 'FAQ' or 'Frequently Asked Questions' section of the User Guide
steps.expectedResult: The FAQ section loads with a list of questions displayed in a collapsed/accordion format, showing only the question text with expand indicators

steps.action: Click on the first FAQ question to expand it
steps.expectedResult: The answer expands below the question with a smooth animation. The answer contains clear, helpful text and may include links to relevant documentation sections

steps.action: Click on the same FAQ question again to collapse it
steps.expectedResult: The answer collapses back, returning to the compact view showing only the question text

steps.action: Click on multiple FAQ questions to expand them simultaneously
steps.expectedResult: Multiple FAQ answers can be expanded at the same time (or if single-expand mode, the previously expanded answer collapses when a new one is opened — behavior should be consistent)

steps.action: Verify that FAQ answers containing links navigate to the correct documentation sections
steps.expectedResult: Clicking a link within an FAQ answer navigates to the referenced documentation section or external resource, opening external links in a new tab

postconditions: All FAQ questions have corresponding answers that are accurate and helpful
FAQ section is easy to navigate and scan for relevant questions
Internal links within FAQ answers point to valid, existing documentation pages

functional.title: Verify documentation is accessible to different user roles with appropriate content visibility
preconditions: Three test accounts exist with different roles: Admin, Developer, and Viewer
Documentation portal has role-based content visibility configured
All three accounts are active and can log in

steps.action: Log in with the 'Viewer' role account and navigate to the documentation portal
steps.expectedResult: The User Guide is accessible. The API documentation may be visible but with limited detail (e.g., no admin-only endpoints shown), or fully visible depending on the access policy

steps.action: Log out and log in with the 'Developer' role account, then navigate to the documentation portal
steps.expectedResult: Both the User Guide and full API documentation are accessible, including all public and developer-level endpoints, code examples, and authentication instructions

steps.action: Log out and log in with the 'Admin' role account, then navigate to the documentation portal
steps.expectedResult: Full documentation is accessible including any admin-only sections such as system configuration endpoints, user management APIs, and administrative guides

steps.action: As Admin, verify that admin-only API endpoints (e.g., 'DELETE /api/v1/users/{id}', 'PUT /api/v1/system/config') are documented and visible
steps.expectedResult: Admin-only endpoints are visible with full documentation including required admin permissions noted in the endpoint description

steps.action: Log back in as 'Viewer' and attempt to access an admin-only documentation URL directly (if applicable)
steps.expectedResult: The admin-only content is either not displayed (hidden) or the user sees a message indicating insufficient permissions to view that section

postconditions: Each role sees documentation appropriate to their access level
No sensitive admin-only API details are exposed to lower-privilege roles (if role-based docs are implemented)
All users can access the general User Guide regardless of role

functional.title: Verify API documentation 'Try It Out' or interactive API console functionality
preconditions: User is logged in with 'Developer' role and on the API documentation page
The documentation includes an interactive 'Try It Out' or API console feature (e.g., Swagger UI, Redoc with try-it)
User has a valid API token or can authenticate within the console
A test/sandbox environment is available for API calls

steps.action: Navigate to a GET endpoint (e.g., 'GET /api/v1/users') in the API documentation
steps.expectedResult: The endpoint detail page includes a 'Try It Out' button or an interactive request builder section

steps.action: Click the 'Try It Out' button
steps.expectedResult: The endpoint section transforms into an interactive form with editable fields for path parameters, query parameters, and headers. An 'Execute' or 'Send' button appears

steps.action: Enter the required authentication token in the Authorization header field (or use the 'Authorize' button at the top of the page to set it globally)
steps.expectedResult: The authentication token is accepted and stored for the session. A lock icon or 'Authorized' indicator confirms the token is set

steps.action: Fill in any required parameters and click the 'Execute' or 'Send' button
steps.expectedResult: The API call is made and the response is displayed below the request section, showing: HTTP status code, response headers, and formatted response body (JSON)

steps.action: Verify the response matches the documented response schema for that endpoint
steps.expectedResult: The actual response fields, data types, and structure match the documented response schema exactly

steps.action: Click the 'Clear' or 'Reset' button to reset the interactive form
steps.expectedResult: All entered parameters are cleared, the response section is hidden, and the form returns to its initial state

postconditions: Interactive API console successfully sends requests and displays responses
API calls from the console hit the correct environment (sandbox/test, not production)
Authentication token is not persisted after the browser session ends

functional.title: Verify documentation can be downloaded or exported as PDF
preconditions: User is on the documentation portal (API docs or User Guide)
A 'Download PDF' or 'Export' option is available on the documentation page
User has permissions to download documentation

steps.action: Locate the 'Download PDF' or 'Export' button on the documentation page (typically in the header, sidebar, or footer)
steps.expectedResult: A 'Download PDF', 'Export', or printer icon button is visible and clickable

steps.action: Click the 'Download PDF' button for the API documentation
steps.expectedResult: A PDF file begins downloading (or a print-friendly preview opens). The file name includes the documentation title and version (e.g., 'API_Documentation_v2.0.pdf')

steps.action: Open the downloaded PDF file and verify its contents
steps.expectedResult: The PDF contains all API documentation sections including: table of contents, authentication, endpoints, error codes, and rate limiting. Formatting is clean with proper page breaks, headers, and code block formatting

steps.action: Verify the PDF includes a generated date and version number on the cover page or header
steps.expectedResult: The PDF displays the generation date and API version number, allowing users to verify the document's currency

steps.action: Repeat the download process for the User Guide
steps.expectedResult: The User Guide PDF downloads successfully with all sections, screenshots, and formatting intact

postconditions: PDF files are generated correctly and contain complete documentation
Downloaded PDFs are readable and properly formatted for printing
PDF file sizes are reasonable (not excessively large due to uncompressed images)

functional.title: Verify documentation links and cross-references are not broken
preconditions: User is on the documentation portal
Documentation contains internal cross-references between sections and external links
All documentation pages have been published

steps.action: Navigate through the API documentation and identify all internal cross-reference links (e.g., 'See Authentication section', 'Refer to Error Codes')
steps.expectedResult: Internal links are visually distinguishable (underlined, colored, or with link icons) and are clickable

steps.action: Click on at least 5 different internal cross-reference links across various sections
steps.expectedResult: Each link navigates to the correct target section within the documentation. No 404 errors or broken link pages are encountered

steps.action: Identify and click on external links (e.g., links to third-party libraries, RFC specifications, or external tools)
steps.expectedResult: External links open in a new browser tab and navigate to the correct external resource. No broken or outdated external links are found

steps.action: Navigate through the User Guide and click on at least 5 internal links
steps.expectedResult: All internal links in the User Guide navigate to the correct sections without errors

steps.action: Check the browser console for any 404 errors related to documentation resources (images, stylesheets, scripts)
steps.expectedResult: No 404 errors appear in the browser console. All resources load successfully

postconditions: All internal and external links in both API documentation and User Guide are functional
No broken links or 404 errors exist in the documentation
External links open in new tabs to prevent users from losing their place in the documentation

functional.title: Verify documentation renders correctly on mobile devices and tablets
preconditions: Documentation portal is accessible via mobile browser
Test devices include: smartphone (iOS Safari, Android Chrome) and tablet (iPad Safari)
Documentation uses responsive design

steps.action: Open the API documentation page on a smartphone browser (or use browser DevTools mobile emulation at 375x812 resolution)
steps.expectedResult: The documentation page loads with a responsive layout. The sidebar/TOC collapses into a hamburger menu or bottom navigation. Content is readable without horizontal scrolling

steps.action: Tap the hamburger menu or navigation toggle to access the table of contents
steps.expectedResult: The TOC slides in from the side or expands as an overlay, showing all sections. Tapping a section navigates to it and closes the menu

steps.action: Scroll through an endpoint documentation section on the mobile device
steps.expectedResult: Code examples wrap or scroll horizontally within their containers. Text is legible at default zoom. Images scale to fit the screen width

steps.action: Test the 'Copy' button on a code example using the mobile device
steps.expectedResult: The copy button is tappable (minimum 44x44px touch target) and copies the code to the mobile clipboard. A visual confirmation appears

steps.action: Open the User Guide on a tablet in landscape orientation
steps.expectedResult: The User Guide displays with an optimal layout for tablet — sidebar TOC may be visible alongside content. Screenshots and images are appropriately sized

steps.action: Rotate the tablet to portrait orientation
steps.expectedResult: The layout adjusts smoothly to portrait mode without content being cut off or overlapping. The TOC may collapse to accommodate the narrower width

postconditions: Documentation is fully usable on mobile and tablet devices
No content is hidden or inaccessible on smaller screens
Touch interactions (tap, scroll, swipe) work correctly throughout the documentation

functional.title: Verify API documentation request/response schema definitions are complete and accurate
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page
At least 3 endpoints with complex request/response bodies are documented
Schema definitions include nested objects and arrays

steps.action: Navigate to a POST endpoint that accepts a complex request body (e.g., 'POST /api/v1/projects')
steps.expectedResult: The endpoint documentation displays a 'Request Body' section with a schema definition table or expandable tree structure

steps.action: Verify the request body schema includes: field name, data type, required/optional flag, description, and constraints (min/max length, regex pattern, enum values)
steps.expectedResult: Each field in the schema is documented with all attributes. For example: 'name' (string, required, max 255 characters), 'status' (string, optional, enum: ['active', 'inactive', 'archived'])

steps.action: Verify nested object schemas are expandable and fully documented
steps.expectedResult: Nested objects (e.g., 'address' containing 'street', 'city', 'zip') are expandable with their own field definitions, data types, and constraints

steps.action: Navigate to the response schema for the same endpoint and verify it documents all response fields
steps.expectedResult: The response schema lists all fields returned by the API including: id, created_at, updated_at, and all input fields echoed back, with data types and descriptions

steps.action: Compare the documented schema against an actual API response by making a test request
steps.expectedResult: The actual API response contains exactly the fields documented in the schema, with matching data types and no undocumented fields

steps.action: Verify that pagination response schema is documented for list endpoints (e.g., 'GET /api/v1/projects')
steps.expectedResult: List endpoints document pagination fields such as 'total', 'page', 'per_page', 'total_pages', and the 'data' array containing the resource objects

postconditions: All request and response schemas are complete, accurate, and match the actual API behavior
No undocumented fields exist in actual API responses
Schema definitions are consistent in format across all endpoints
